correctness.rationale: An exact unitary Zak/Parseval decomposition gives F_q=sum of q squared Zak translates. The independent geometric-series Poisson Zak identity is explicit and valid for all w>0. For any frequency the multiplier is strictly increasing in cos(2pi x) by a positive derivative. The reduced frequency sum is strictly convex, so the unique extrema and exact hyperbolic formulas follow. At the lower fiber a positive sum of q squared differences cannot vanish for q>=2. Taylor/exponential asymptotic expansions give the exact constants for each fixed q. Standard-library numerical checks compare direct lattice Zak values, algebraic endpoints and closed forms.

value.rationale: The Poisson window is a canonical rational two-pole time-frequency generator. Sharp optimal bounds for every integer redundancy q>=2 are directly motivated by stable reconstruction; qualitative frame membership does not determine them. The theorem gives explicit universal formulas, unique extremal Zak fibers, and two sharply contrasting conditioning laws with leading coefficients. It is not an arbitrary numerical case, textbook normalization substitution or small improvement to a known constant.
